design_rationale:
WORKLOG task 1 (personal_payments_limits_and_account_access, category wallet). frozen_time 2026-10-08 14:40:00 ET.
[Step 0 draw] draw_counts.py --task 1 -> {"prerequisite_problems": 1, "problems": 2, "factor_counts": [4, 5]}. Prerequisite wallet_ext_protection_reimbursement takes 4 factors, root wallet_ext_claim_money_instant_fee takes 5. One prerequisite -> one value_input edge required; the single edge is value_input.
[Scope snapshot] Occupied by task 0: wallet_ext_renewal_plan_fee / charge_plan_fee_0f985a0a and wallet_ext_available_balance_transfer / transfer_balance_to_bank_3181bc35. Claimed now: wallet_ext_protection_reimbursement (subject wallet_claim_reimbursement, tool post_protection_reimbursement_5be5cf5a, agent) and wallet_ext_claim_money_instant_fee (subjects wallet_cash_out + wallet_fee, tool send_instant_cash_out_cd9063e1, user). Disjoint from task 0 in policies, tools, subjects and computation family. This is the last task; the union of the two scopes is all four extended policies.
[Design thesis] Surface goal: 'my claim on the amp got approved, push that money to my debit card instantly'. Scored values: the reimbursement owed on the approved purchase protection claim (4 factors) and the instant transfer fee on sending it (5 factors). Chain: surface goal -> the instant fee rule's prerequisite sentence ('An instant cash-out of claim money is priced only after the purchase protection claim most recently approved on the account carries its reimbursement entry.') -> the claim record shows approved 2026-10-06, no provisional credit, and the activity shows no reimbursement entry -> the only write booking a reimbursement entry is the protection reimbursement policy's -> compute it, book it -> the transfer amount is that reimbursement and the balance rises -> compute the fee -> hand the transfer over. Breadth: the reimbursement reads the claim, the disputed payment, its funding fee, the seller's payments back, the account age, the claim filings of up to twelve months, the claim's report and approval dates and the rewards membership; the fee reads three deposit windows, the quota count, the card (status, activation), the balance and the savings vault.
[Why a good test] The customer believes the money is already his to send; the agent must discover from the policy that the reimbursement entry is missing, compute a reimbursement whose covered amount nets a proportional funding fee in and the seller's refund out, whose coverage share depends on a look-back window chosen by account age, which carries a claim-review delay credit and whose ceiling is raised by the rewards tier; and then price an instant transfer whose rate stacks a deposit tier chosen through an age-dependent averaging window with two cuts and a saver reduction. Baseline-only readers get 2500.00 and 25.00; skipping the reimbursement gives a 0.23 fee.
[Base-invariant card] Reimbursement (subject wallet_claim_reimbursement): governing wallet_unauthorized_claims (one-claim-per-payment exclusion; its gates apply to filing and provisional credit only) and wallet_purchase_protection (protection_window applies to filing) -> both policy_scope for this write; the claim on payment 2026-08-14 was filed 2026-09-02 (19 days, inside 180) and approved by the claims team on 2026-10-06 with provisional_credit_posted false; exactly one claim on that payment. Overwrite: the base sentence '... an approval reimburses the lower of the claim amount and purchase_protection_max_amount as a wallet_claim_reimbursement, together with the refund of any credit card funding fee ...' is superseded (same world: base 2500.00 plus a separate 95.40 fee refund; extended one entry of 2722.76). Instant cash-out (subjects wallet_cash_out, wallet_fee): wallet_cash_out_rules.cash_out_status satisfied (status active, bound to wallet_id); wallet_instant_transfer_fee, wallet_plan_fee, wallet_funding_fees, wallet_evt_receiving policy_scope; Core instant maximum 5000.00, daily limit 5000.00 (no cash-out dated 2026-10-08), 2722.76 + 15.93 <= 3963.31. Overwrites on wallet_instant_transfer_fee: the calendar-month quota sentence, the previous-calendar-month rate sentence and the fee formula sentence (same world: a calendar-month quota would be unused in October -> fee 0.00; the extended rolling month counts the 2026-09-20 instant transfer -> fee 15.93). No time gate applies to either write (temporal_feasibility []).
[Business-object card] Target claim: the resolved (approved 2026-10-06) purchase protection claim on the 3180.00 goods-and-services payment to @vintage_amp_61; its funding fee row (95.40, points to the payment); the seller's 300.00 personal payment back. Excluded from the claim paid: the 2025-11-14 payment to @cable_depot_61 and the 2026-02-12 payment to @gadget_bin_61, whose claims were denied (they only count as filings in the look-back window), rent and friend payments, the standard cash-outs to the bank ending 1907. The reimbursement entry points to the amplifier payment. The instant transfer goes to the card ending 1588 (same as the 2026-09-20 instant cash-out, which is the one transfer in the quota window).
[Problem-tree card] root wallet_ext_claim_money_instant_fee <- wallet_ext_protection_reimbursement; kind value_input; gate reimb_amt (and the ledger read by the balance cut); form state; affirmative direction ('is priced only after'), the way a fee desk states when a price can be quoted, unlike task 0's 'not ... until'; policy_source as quoted above. Four-point test: 'only after'; a record-visible state (a reimbursement entry on the most recently approved purchase protection claim); no tool, id or code token; a hard requirement scoped to that one claim, the same claim the reimbursement rule pays. Exactly one write of the difficulty books a claim reimbursement entry (post_protection_reimbursement_5be5cf5a). Derivation: sentence + the latest approved claim record (approved, no provisional credit) + activity (no reimbursement) + the reimbursement rule ('an approval is paid as one reimbursement entry pointing to the disputed payment') -> book the reimbursement. Unresolved at frozen_time: resolution approved, provisional_credit_posted False, no wallet_claim_reimbursement row. Deletion sensitivity (run): skip step 7 -> fee 0.23 (reimb_amt 0.00, balance cut 0), and the terminal DB lacks the 2722.76 credit. The root is owned by the customer (user tool: he sends his own money and accepts the fee).
[Factor card — protection reimbursement, baseline 'covered amount capped at purchase_protection_max_amount' = min(2975.40, 2500.00) = 2500.00] The funding fee part (fee x claim / payment = 95.40) and the seller-money deduction (personal in full, goods-and-services net of the seller fee = 300.00) are one fixed formula each inside the baseline, not factors. claim_lookback_window (parameter, date — relabelled from method in round 3: its tiers only choose the window length N): 475-day account -> nine-month window -> one other claim (2026-02-19); six months -> 0 claims -> 3025.29, twelve months (baseline) -> 2 claims -> 2420.23; near miss: the 2025-11-20 claim is inside twelve months but outside nine. repeat_claim_share (parameter, history): one other claim -> 90 percent; baseline 100 -> 3025.29. claim_review_delay_credit (method, date + claim record): reported 2026-09-02, approved 2026-10-06, 34 days -> tier 1 algorithm, simple interest at 18 percent a year on the amount after the share, actual/365: 2677.86 x 0.18 x 34 / 365 = 44.900009; tier 2's algorithm is a flat 1 percent (26.78 -> 2704.64) and the fall-through adds nothing (2677.86) — an accrual, a flat percentage and nothing cannot be written as one formula with a substituted constant. rewards_protection_multiplier (parameter, cross-difficulty rewards; status and tier of one membership row): active Gold -> 1.5 -> ceiling 3750.00; baseline 2500.00. Result 2975.40 x 0.90 = 2677.86 + 44.900009 = 2722.760009 -> 2722.76 < 3750.00. The repeat-claim share deliberately counts filings of any outcome as an abuse signal.
[Factor card — instant fee, baseline 'amount x instant_transfer_fee_rate_pct clamped' = 25.00] deposit_rate_tier (parameter, history; the one multi-source factor of this computation: the direct deposit measure and the one-month deposit count read different deposit sets): measure 5200.00 and 2 deposits -> 1.00; baseline 22.50. deposit_measure_window (method, redesigned in round 3): 475-day account -> the middle value of the last three monthly totals (1800.00, 5200.00, 5200.00 -> 5200.00); the mid-tenure algorithm takes the lower of the last two monthly totals (1800.00) and the fall-through the last month's total (1800.00) — a median, a minimum and a single total are different aggregates, not one formula with a constant; baseline 22.50. card_tenure_cut (parameter, cross-difficulty card; status and activation date of one card row): active since 2025-07-05 -> 0.25; baseline 22.05. balance_rate_cut (parameter; balance and opened date of the one account row): 3963.31 after the reimbursement -> 0.10 (without it 1240.55 -> 0); baseline 18.38. saver_fee_reduction (parameter, cross-difficulty savings): vault 1500.00 -> 10 percent; baseline 17.70. Quota plumbing: 0 + 1 card bonus = 1; the 2026-09-20 instant transfer (fee 0.00, inside the quota then) uses it — the discriminating record, since a reader of the superseded calendar-month quota drops it and prices 0.00. Result 2722.76 x 0.65 percent = 17.69794 -> x 0.90 = 15.92815 -> 15.93.
[Seed rows and why] customer; Core account opened 2025-06-20 (age for the look-back window, the deposit window and the balance cut); 21 activity rows summing to ledger 1240.55: six payroll deposits (2600 x 4, then 900 x 2 — the window trap), the amplifier payment with its credit-card funding pull and 3.00 percent fee, the seller's personal 300.00, two earlier goods payments (88.00 on 2025-11-14, 145.00 on 2026-02-12), rent and other payments, two standard cash-outs, one instant cash-out with its 0.00 fee; six claim rows (the denied November and February claims filed and resolved; the amplifier claim filed and approved); card (quota bonus, tenure cut), rewards Gold (ceiling), savings vault 1500.00 (saver reduction). Automatic clauses checked: no unclaimed invitation, no returned cash-out, no plan fee (Core), the approved claim owes exactly the reimbursement this task books, nothing pending in other products.
[Persona] Rafael is talkative and in a hurry for a weekend gig. He opens with the claim-money request and gives identity and card digits only when asked. He knows the approval from the app, which matches the claim record, and does not know any amounts. When asked, he says the seller sent back 300 dollars and that two earlier small claims were turned down. His passive reactions: he agrees when told the money must first be credited, asks once whether the fee is really that, sends exactly what he is handed, and hangs up on the transfer receipt.
[Standard solution] find_customers(5552618817) -> verify (phone, DOB, SSN four) -> read account, claims, activity, rewards -> unlock + call post_protection_reimbursement_5be5cf5a(wallet, amplifier payment, 2722.76) -> read card, vaults -> unlock user tool -> customer calls send_instant_cash_out_cd9063e1(wallet, 2722.76, 1588, 15.93).
[Verification run] A recompute script replayed the gold with the real tools and evaluated each compute at its handling time with check_compute's evaluator: reimbursement 2722.76 at step 7; fee 15.93 at step 11 after it; factor substitution figures as above; skip-edge fee 0.23. Gates were run per task with --task 1 and then difficulty-wide (outputs in the difficulty worklog).
[Solvability vs GT] step 7 is state_due (evidence: the approved claim record, provisional_credit_posted false); step 11 is on_request (customer line 'my claim on the amp got approved, and I want that money pushed to my debit card instantly, today'); cash_out_status is bound to wallet_id; the stage provenance of step 11 is prior_step 7.
[Draft recomputation from the visible context] Reading only the published rules: the fee rule's sentence sends the agent to the most recently approved claim, which has no reimbursement; the reimbursement rule gives (3180.00 + 95.40 - 300.00) x 90 percent (nine-month window, one other claim) = 2677.86, plus 18 percent a year for 34 review days (44.90) = 2722.76 under a 3750.00 ceiling; the fee rule gives the median monthly deposit total 5200.00 -> tier 1.00, rate 1.00 - 0.25 - 0.10 = 0.65 on 2722.76 = 17.70 inside the clamp, less 10 percent = 15.93 — identical to gold.
[Revisions] r3 (audit round 4, T1-F3/T1-O5): the delay-credit intermediate is 2677.86 x 0.18 x 34 / 365 = 44.900009 (the proof had 44.8957) and the pre-rounding reimbursement is 2722.760009 (the proof had 2722.7557), corrected in the factor card, factor_trace and argument tracing; the factor_trace label of claim_review_delay_credit now reads method, as in the charter. Scored values unchanged (2722.76, 15.93). r1 (audit round 2, F-1/F-2/T1-F1): funding_fee_part and seller_return_deduction were one formula written as three tiers. Both became fixed baseline formulas, and two honest factors replaced them: claim_lookback_window (method: 6 / 9 / 12-month look-back by account age; the tiers give 3034.91 / 2722.76 / 2427.93 on this world) and claim_review_delay_credit (parameter: 2 / 1 / 0 percent by days from report to approval). An 88.00 goods payment with a denied 2025-11-20 claim was seeded as the window's near miss, and the 2026-09-28 payment was reduced from 969.05 to 881.05 so the ledger stays 1240.55. New values: reimbursement 2722.76, fee 15.93. O-5: the paid claim is 'the purchase protection claim most recently approved', and the other-claims count now subtracts the paid claim's own filing within the same window instead of subtracting 1. O-10: the rule states that a return carries the speed of the transfer it returns (base event field). O-11: the rate sentence now reads 'Whatever deposit rate tier applies ... (each cut being 0 where it does not apply)'. T1-O2: the rationale was '(pending)' on disk and is now complete. T1-O3: the discriminating quota record (2026-09-20 instant transfer) is named in the factor card. r2 (audit round 3, F2-1/T1-F2): under the auditor's calibration a method tier must change the algorithm, not substitute a constant. claim_lookback_window is relabelled parameter; claim_review_delay_credit became the method (simple interest at 18 percent a year, actual/365, on 30+ review days; a flat 1 percent at 15-29 days; none below); deposit_measure_window now takes the median of the last three monthly totals (365+ days), the lower of the last two (180-364 days) or the last month's total. New values: reimbursement 2722.76, fee 15.93. O2-2: the prerequisite sentence now waits on 'the purchase protection claim most recently approved on the account', the same claim the reimbursement rule pays, and the condition names the latest approved row. T1-O4: multi-source is claimed only for deposit_rate_tier; card_tenure_cut and balance_rate_cut are labelled as one-record factors.
user_scenario: You are Rafael Dunmore, a 38-year-old live-sound engineer in Austin, friendly and talkative but a bit impatient today. Back in August you bought a vintage guitar amplifier through Pocketwire as a goods-and-services purchase and it arrived dead; you filed a purchase protection claim, and on Tuesday the app told you the claim was approved. You are calling because you want that claim money on your bank debit card right away, by instant transfer, because you have a gig out of town this weekend. You know an instant transfer has a fee and you are fine paying it; you want to send it yourself from the app once the representative tells you the fee. You open with something like: "Hey — my claim on the amp got approved, and I want that money pushed to my debit card instantly, today." When asked who you are, you give your mobile number, 5552618817. Only when asked for more to confirm it is you do you give your date of birth, November 2, 1987 (1987-11-02), and then the last four of your Social Security number, 1276, one at a time. Only when asked which card, you say it is your credit union debit card ending in 1588, the same one you sent money to last month. You do not know the exact amount Pocketwire approved and you do not know your current balance; if asked, you say you'd rather they check. If asked whether the seller gave anything back, you say he sent you 300 dollars through the app for a missing part, before you filed. If asked whether you ever filed claims before, you say yes, two small ones that were turned down — a cable order last November and a gadget in February. If asked about other Pocketwire products, you mention your Pocketwire debit card, your rewards membership and a savings vault you call Studio gear. If the representative tells you the claim money still has to be put on your balance before it can be sent, you say go ahead. When the representative tells you the amount and the fee, you do not haggle; if the fee sounds high you ask once whether that is really the fee and accept the answer. When the representative hands you the transfer to send, you send exactly the amount, card and fee they give you. As soon as you see the instant transfer went through, you thank them and hang up. You do not ask for anything else, you do not ask for a human, and you never suggest what the amount or the fee should be.
